rmt-2011-adv-01.title: Geometric series
rmt-2011-adv-01.body:
Of the 36 outcomes, 21 have sum greater than 6, so each throw wins with probability $\frac{21}{36}=\frac7{12}$ and fails with probability $\frac5{12}$. The mathematician wins on his $k$-th throw if all $2(k-1)$ earlier throws fail, so
$$P=\frac7{12}\sum_{k\ge0}\left(\frac5{12}\right)^{2k}=\frac{7/12}{1-25/144}=\frac7{12}\cdot\frac{144}{119}=\frac{12}{17}.$$

**Answer: $\frac{12}{17}$**

rmt-2011-adv-01.title: Recursion
rmt-2011-adv-01.body:
Let $P$ be the probability that the player about to throw eventually wins. He wins at once with probability $\frac7{12}$; otherwise ($\frac5{12}$) the opponent becomes the player about to throw and wins with probability $P$. So $P=\frac7{12}+\frac5{12}(1-P)$, giving $\frac{17}{12}P=1$ and $P=\frac{12}{17}$.

**Answer: $\frac{12}{17}$**

rmt-2011-adv-06.title: Expected value
rmt-2011-adv-06.body:
This is the expected value of a binomial random variable with $n=2011$ trials and success probability $p=\frac13$, so it equals $np=\frac{2011}3$.

**Answer: $\frac{2011}{3}$**
